lease.name: run
lease.summary: LAST RESORT for JavaScript. Prefer an ordinary code block, which is instant and free; this starts a container that is billed by the second while it runs and only for its storage while it is paused, and it cannot call your other tools. Use it only when you genuinely need npm packages, a real filesystem, or more than a few seconds of compute. The container is NOT the per-execution sandbox: every call uses the same one, in this turn and later ones, so installs and files survive from one call to the next — do not reinstall. It stays until you release it; after 30 idle minutes it is paused, keeping its memory, running processes and files, and billed only for its storage until the next call resumes it where it was; it is deleted, with everything on its disk, 24 hours after it was created whatever it is doing, and nothing postpones that: `keep` the environment or `save` the files you will want after then; `quiet` postpones the pause by as long as you choose, within the mount's limit. Work in as few calls as you can, save what matters with `save`, and release it once the machine will not be needed again. Releasing deletes it and everything on its disk. Every call uses the mount's one machine unless you pass `machine`: another short name is a separate container with its own files, directory and idle schedule, created on first use and released on its own. Use one unless you need two at once; at most a few (3 unless the operator set `maxMachines`) may exist at once, switched-off ones included, and `machines` lists them.

lease.name: shell
lease.summary: Shell in the same container as `run`, billed by the second while it runs, and the same one for every call, in this turn and later ones — state, installed packages and files carry over — until you release it; after 30 idle minutes it is paused, keeping its memory, running processes and files, and billed only for its storage until the next call resumes it where it was; it is deleted, with everything on its disk, 24 hours after it was created whatever it is doing, and nothing postpones that: `keep` the environment or `save` the files you will want after then; `quiet` postpones the pause by as long as you choose, within the mount's limit. Each call starts in the directory the previous call ended in, like one terminal session, and its result says where that is (`cwd`); the first starts in the working directory. Pass `workdir` to run one command in another directory instead of starting it with `cd`. Exported variables and aliases do not carry over, so set them in the command that needs them, and a command handed over as a job does not move the directory. Only for what needs a real machine (builds, tests, git). The default template is universal (Debian 13): Node, npm, git, curl, make, gcc/g++, Python 3, pip, jq, gh, Go, Docker, bash, ssh, apt-get and sudo are present; rg are NOT, and `sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y <pkg>` installs more. An operator may have configured a different image; every result reports which one this container started from, so read that instead of probing for it. Save anything worth keeping, then release. Every call uses the mount's one machine unless you pass `machine`: another short name is a separate container with its own files, directory and idle schedule, created on first use and released on its own. Use one unless you need two at once; at most a few (3 unless the operator set `maxMachines`) may exist at once, switched-off ones included, and `machines` lists them.

lease.name: save
lease.summary: Copy a file out of the container into durable storage before it is destroyed. Returns an r2:// reference the artifacts mount can read back, and that outlives the box. Set archive for a directory. Do this for anything worth keeping — a build output, a report, a diff — the moment it exists, not at the end. A copy outliving the container is not a reason to release it: if you or the person you are working for will come back to this machine, leave it running — idle, it is only paused, and the next call resumes it with its files and running processes.

lease.name: put
lease.summary: Copy a stored file into the container, so a command there can work on it. `ref` is an artifact:// reference of yours: what an attachment download or `save` returned. The usual way to process an attachment is: download it (attachments_download_url), `put` it here, work on it with `shell` or `run`, `save` the result, then view or upload what `save` returned. No URLs: anything from outside arrives through a download first. At most 25 MiB. Returns the path, size and sha256 as the container has it. An existing file at the path is replaced.

lease.name: keep
lease.summary: Save this container's filesystem under a name, so a later task can start from it instead of installing everything again. Use it once the environment is set up — interpreter, packages, a cloned repository — not for the results, which belong in `save`. The container keeps running; the snapshot is independent of it. A copy outliving the container is not a reason to release it: if you or the person you are working for will come back to this machine, leave it running — idle, it is only paused, and the next call resumes it with its files and running processes.

lease.name: start_from
lease.summary: Begin from an environment kept earlier instead of a bare image. Naming one releases the current container if there is one; the next run or shell starts from the snapshot. Call with no name to see what has been kept, which releases nothing. Setting up a machine is usually the slowest and most expensive part of using one, and this is how you stop paying for it twice. Pass `machine` to start that machine from it instead of the default one; kept environments are shared by all of the mount's machines.

lease.name: release
lease.summary: Delete the container now: the machine and everything on its disk are destroyed, and the meter stops. Pass save to copy files out first, in the same call. If you or the person you are working for will come back to it, leave it running, even after keeping or saving what is in it. Release it only when this machine will not be needed again. Leaving it costs little: an idle container is only paused on its own, and the next call resumes it where it was; it is deleted on its own 24 hours after it was created at the latest, which nothing postpones — while releasing it early saves little and makes the next visit start over. A kept environment or a saved file is for starting a fresh machine later, not a reason to destroy one someone will use again.

lease.name: quiet
lease.summary: Postpone what happens next to this container while it sits unused: pausing it, while it is running; deleting it, once it is paused. It is kept as it is for at least `minutes` more from now, and you are not told about it again until shortly before then. It does not postpone the deletion 24 hours after the container was created. Use it when you are coming back to the machine — a build you are waiting on, work you return to after reading something. The limit is the mount's while it runs and much longer once it is paused. Running, it is billed for every second either way; if you are done with it, `release` is the cheaper answer, and it can save files out in the same call.

lease.name: machines
lease.summary: List this mount's machines: each one's name, whether it is running or paused, its template, when it was created and last used, when it will be paused or deleted if nothing uses it, and when it is deleted regardless. Reads the record only; starts, wakes and bills nothing.
